title: Exception policy + override UX for Optimize quality gates (approvers, time bounds, audit representation)
creator: Aditya Rao
content:
Context
Optimize will block applying cost-saving config diffs (batching policy, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile) unless required quality gates pass. We need a clear, consistent exception policy for when teams must ship despite a failing/inconclusive gate, and a UX+audit representation that is safe-by-default and enterprise-auditable.

This ticket defines:
1) Exception/override rules (who/when/how)
2) Approver model + RBAC alignment
3) Console UX states & copy
4) Audit log representation (fields, events)
5) Operational guardrails (expiration, follow-ups, notifications)

Drivers
- Near-miss: a proposed optimization almost shipped without adequate review (see #incidents thread 1764369002 and Ava Chen email 2026-02-03). Leadership direction: overrides must be rarer, time-bound, and auditable; “override as a path” should feel intentionally painful.
- Enterprise prospects are explicitly asking “who can change inference behavior” and want immutable logs (security review call transcript 2026-02-06).

Policy proposal (v1, hosted API / Dedicated defaults)

A. When overrides are allowed
1) Allowed reasons (must choose one):
   - Production incident mitigation: need cost reduction to avoid capacity exhaustion / elevated error rates
   - False positive / eval flakiness suspected (with evidence)
   - Non-user-facing workload: internal route, offline batch job, or sandbox environment
   - Customer-approved risk: written acknowledgment from customer owner for a time-bounded window
2) Not allowed:
   - “We want to ship” / schedule pressure
   - Repeated overrides for the same prompt set / model family without mitigation plan
   - Overrides on self-serve tiers (no enterprise contract) unless incident mitigation is declared by oncall

B. Scope & blast-radius restrictions
- Overrides must be scoped to a single route (route_id) and config change (diff_id). No “global” overrides.
- Overrides may only unlock canary enablement; canary promotion to 100% still requires either:
  - gates pass, OR
  - a second approval + explicit customer impact statement (see Approvers)
- Quantization profile overrides require stricter handling:
  - Must attach artifacts for long-context coverage (if applicable)
  - Must include runtime compatibility check result (static validation pass)

C. Expiration
- Default expiration: 24 hours.
- Maximum expiration: 7 days (enterprise only), requires additional approver.
- Overrides auto-expire and revert state to “blocked” unless gate later passes.
- Post-expiration: Console must show “Expired override” and require a fresh request.

D. Evidence requirements (minimum)
- Link to gate run (gate_run_id)
- A short narrative (free text, 3–10 sentences)
- At least one of:
  - rerun result (or flake score) OR
  - canary plan (traffic %, duration, rollback trigger) OR
  - incident ticket link
- For “false positive / flakiness”: must attach rerun attempt or quarantine rationale.

Approver model (RBAC)

We need two axes: internal Redwood operators vs customer operators.

1) Internal Redwood (hosted / Dedicated managed by Redwood)
- Requester: Optimize route owner (any user with Optimize:Write on that route)
- Approver levels:
  - Level 1 (standard): Oncall SRE (or designated “Quality Gate Override Approver” role)
  - Level 2 (high-risk): Applied ML manager OR Runtime safety architect depending on config type

Approval matrix (v1)
- Batching / caching diffs:
  - Up to 24h, canary-only: Level 1
  - >24h or promote beyond 25%: Level 1 + Level 2
- Quantization profile diffs:
  - Any override: Level 1 + Level 2 (Runtime safety)
  - >24h: Level 1 + Level 2 + Product sponsor sign-off (Marissa Cole or delegate)

2) Customer-managed (Private/on-prem later)
- v1 policy will be documented but enforcement is manual. Console should still represent override events and include approver identity even if approvals happen in the customer’s ITSM.

Console UX requirements

States (surface everywhere Optimize shows recommendations + config history)
- Gate status: Pending | Running | Passed | Failed | Inconclusive (flake/timeout) | Quarantined (suite)
- Apply CTA states:
  - Enabled: Passed
  - Disabled w/ reason: Failed / Inconclusive / Quarantined
  - Enabled with banner: Override granted (show expiry + approver)

Override flow (proposed)
1) “Request override” button appears only when apply is blocked.
2) Modal/flow fields:
   - Reason dropdown (policy reasons)
   - Expiration selector (default 24h; max shown based on user + config type)
   - Scope confirmation (route + diff summary; traffic cap slider if canary)
   - Evidence links (gate run + incident/customer approval)
   - Required checkbox: “I understand this may degrade quality and will auto-expire.”
3) After submit:
   - State becomes “Override requested”
   - Notification sent to approver queue (Slack + email)
4) Approver view:
   - Clear diff summary (before/after knobs)
   - Gate deltas + confidence indicators (including flake score)
   - Risk tags (quantization/long-context/high variance)
   - Approve / Deny with mandatory comment

UI copy guidelines
- Avoid implying that override is normal. Use “Exception” language in explanatory text.
- Always show expiration prominently.
- Always link to artifacts and runbook (if internal) from the failure/override view.

Audit log representation

We need immutable, queryable events for:
- gate.run.started
- gate.run.completed (include pass/fail/inconclusive + summary metrics)
- gate.override.requested
- gate.override.granted
- gate.override.denied
- gate.override.expired
- gate.override.revoked (manual)
- config.apply.attempted (blocked/allowed + reason)

Minimum audit fields (per event)
- actor_id, actor_type (user/service), actor_role
- route_id, account_id, model_id/model_family, hardware_sku (if relevant)
- diff_id, diff_type (batching|cache|quantization), baseline_ref
- gate_run_id(s)
- decision (approved/denied/expired) + decision_reason_code
- expiry_timestamp
- links: artifact pointers (eval report, traces), incident/customer approval URL

Security considerations
- Overrides must be permissioned via explicit role (separate from general Optimize:Write).
- Approver actions require re-auth (fresh session) for internal Redwood admins.
- All override events must be exportable (SIEM) via existing audit export.

Metrics/Success criteria
- Override rate < 3% of all blocked applies (initial target; revisit after beta)
- Median time to decision < 2 hours during business hours for enterprise routes
- 0 “silent” applies: every apply attempt is either gated-passed or has an override event chain
- Customer feedback from security reviews: audit trail described as “clear and sufficient”

Open questions
1) Do we allow a “temporary allow canary at 1%” without Level 2 for quantization? (currently: no)
2) For timeouts in a region (EU-West), do we treat as Inconclusive with a separate policy path? (recommend: same override path, but reason code “infra-timeout”)
3) Should we require a follow-up task automatically created on override grant (e.g., Linear issue linked)? (recommend: yes, but can be phase 2 if engineering scope tight)

Implementation notes / handoffs
- Align with ENG-3927 on event names/fields.
- Align with ENG-3925/DES-611 on states + UX.
- Align with Sean Gallagher on oncall queue + expected SLA for approvals.

Comments / updates

2026-02-05 (Aditya Rao)
Drafted initial approval matrix. Key call: quantization overrides always require Runtime safety sign-off. Flagged need for separate RBAC role.

2026-02-07 (Sean Gallagher)
+1 on separate role and re-auth for approvers. Oncall can cover Level 1; we need a named fallback when oncall is overloaded. Suggest paging only for incident-mitigation overrides; otherwise async approval.

2026-02-09 (Karthik Iyer)
For “flake suspected,” require at least one rerun attempt unless infra capacity is constrained. Also request that UI shows confidence/variance so approvers aren’t making blind calls.

2026-02-11 (Kenji Nakamura)
Proposed UI copy changes: replace “Override” with “Request exception” and emphasize auto-expiry. Added mock notes to DES-611.

2026-02-13 (Marissa Cole)
Resolved: canary-only exception can unlock up to 10% traffic (default 1% slider) for batching/caching; anything higher uses the promotion gate path.

2026-02-18 (Marcus Lin)
Security review: ensure audit events include both request + decision payload, and that decision comment is mandatory. No objections to policy; recommends documenting export to SIEM for enterprise narrative.

Next steps
- Finalize Level 2 approver routing by diff type (Runtime vs Applied ML) and document in policy.
- Confirm RBAC role name + provisioning workflow (INT-3391 request incoming).
- Update external docs and release notes with customer-facing explanation of exceptions (without exposing internals).
